title: Discrepancy lower bound for public-coin complexity
statement: Let $\mu$ be a finite probability space on $X \times Y$, let $g : X \to Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$, and let $\varepsilon, \gamma \in \bbr$ and $n \in \bbn$. Suppose that every rectangle $R = A \times B \subseteq X \times Y$ satisfies $\abs{\mathrm{disc}_\mu(g, R)} \le \gamma$, where $\mathrm{disc}_\mu(g, R) = \E_{(x,y)\sim\mu}\bigl[\mathbf{1}_R(x,y)\cdot\sigma(g(x,y))\bigr]$ and $\sigma$ sends $\mathrm{false}$ to $1$ and $\mathrm{true}$ to $-1$. If moreover $2^n \cdot \gamma < 1 - 2\varepsilon$, then $n < \mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(g)$, the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of $g$.
hypotheses_covered: finite probability space μ on X × Y
ε, γ real and n natural
replaced:
